subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept the proposed device.publicKey/signature bounds and per-IP device-signature pre-auth lockout as the gateway security boundary for connect handshakes?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but it changes unauthenticated gateway behavior, protocol validation, and availability under failed device-bearing browser-origin handshakes, which needs owner security-policy acceptance.

options.title: Accept Layered Hardening
options.body: Approve the schema bounds, shape prechecks, and pre-crypto limiter as the intended mitigation, then merge after normal owner review.

options.title: Tune Before Merge
options.body: Ask for adjusted bounds, limiter keying, lockout behavior, or PoC placement while keeping the early gate before createPublicKey and verify.

options.title: Pause For Redesign
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want a broader gateway auth redesign instead of another limiter scope.

recommendation.title: Accept Layered Hardening
recommendation.body: Approve the schema bounds, shape prechecks, and pre-crypto limiter as the intended mitigation, then merge after normal owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history across device auth, extracted handshake helpers, and adjacent gateway security hardening.
